Θαδδαῖος, -ου, ὁ (Aram. תּדִאַי, תַּדַּי), 
Thaddæus: Mat.10.3, Mrk.3.18 (WH, mg., Λεββαῖος, which see).†
(AS)

θάλασσα, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly for יָם ;] 
the sea: Mat.23.15, Mrk.11.23, Luk.21.25, Rom.9.27, Heb.11.12, Jas.1.6, Jude.13, Rev.7.1, al.; τὸ πέλαγος τῆς θ. (see Tr., ut infr.), Mat.18.6 ὁ οὐρανὸς κ. ἡ γῆ κ. ἡ θ., of the whole world, Act.4.24, al. (Hag.2.7); θ. ὑαλίνη, Rev.4.6; 15.2; of the Mediterranean, Act.10.6, 32; 17.14; of the Red Sea, ἐρυθρὰ θ., Act.7.36, 1Co.10.1-2, Heb.11.20; of an inland lake (as Heb.…

θάλπω 
[in LXX for סָכַן, etc. ;] 
to heat, warm; metaphorically, 
__(a) to inflame (Trag.); 
__(b) to foster, cherish: Eph.5.29, 1Th.2.7.†
(AS)

Θάμαρ (Tr., Θαμάρ), ἡ (Heb. תָּמָר, Gen.38.6), 
Tamar: Mat.1.3.†
(AS)

θαμβέω, -ῶ
(θάμβος) [in LXX for בָּעַת ni., pi., etc. ;] 
__1. to be amazed. 
__2. In late Gk., to astonish, terrify (2Sa.22.5): pass., Mrk.1.27; 10.32; before ἐπί with dative of thing(s), Mrk.10.24.†
(AS)

θάμβος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX for פַּחַד, etc. ;] 
amazement: Luk.4.36; 5.9, Act.3.10.†
(AS)

θανατη-φόρος, -ον
(θάνατος, φέρω), [in LXX: Num.18.22 (מוּת), Job.33.23, 4Ma.8.18 4Mac.8.26 4Mac.15.26 * ;] 
deadly, death-bringing: Jas.3.8.†
(AS)

θάνατος, -ου, ὁ (θνήσκω), 
[in LXX chiefly for מָוֶת ,מוּת, sometimes דֶּבֶר ;] 
death; 
__1. of the death of the body, whether natural or violent: Jhn.11.13, Php.2.27, Heb.7.23, al; opposite to ζωή, Rom.8.38, Php.1.20; of the death of Christ, Rom.5.10, Php.3.10, Heb.2.9; ῥυέσθαι (σώζειν) ἐκ θ., 2Co.1.10, Heb.5.7; περίλυπος ἕως θανάτου, Mat.26.38, Mrk.14.34; μέχρι (ἄχρι), Php.2.8, Rev.2.10; πληγὴ θανάτου, a deadly…

θανατόω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for מוּת hi., ho., also for הָרַג, etc. ;] 
to put to death: with accusative, Mat.10.21; 26.59; 27.1, Mrk.13.12; 14.55, Luk.21.16, 2Co.6.9, 1Pe.3.18; pass., Rom.8.36. Metaphorical: Rom.8.13 pass., with dative, (in relation to), Rom.7.4.†
(AS)
